title: Environmental Protection Agency news - Today’s latest updates

Nixon first proposed the creation of the US Environmental Protection Agency 9 July 1970. As boring and dry as that factoid might seem, it’s really important right now to understand what the EPA was… | John Pabon
description:
Nixon first proposed the creation of the US Environmental Protection Agency 9 July 1970. As boring and dry as that factoid might seem, it’s really important right now to understand what the EPA was meant to do, its legacy, and why its future is so uncertain.

On paper, the EPA brought together many of the different departments looking at conservation, pollution, and the environment. It was a pretty tangled mess spanning the Interior Department, Health, Education, Welfare, and other places. Nixon wanted them all under one roof sitting within the Executive Branch. The EPA would formally start that December under the leadership of William Ruckelshaus, the man who famously quit rather than follow the orders of Nixon during the Watergate scandal.

Over its history, the EPA has had tremendous success: the Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act frameworks that cut smog and helped rescue rivers like the Cuyahoga, which literally caught fire before EPA existed; the phase-out of leaded gasoline, linked to major drops in childhood lead exposure; and the near-elimination of DDT, which helped bring bald eagles back from the brink. It’s also served as a model for similar agencies around the world.

But all of that is under threat today, with the EPA being gutted by the current administration. Remember, the EPA was never created by its own act of Congress. It exists because Nixon reorganised the executive branch, which is part of why it's so vulnerable. That legacy is now under direct pressure. Since early 2025, the EPA has lost thousands of staff, with workforce levels at their lowest since the 1980s, while the administration has repeatedly cut the agency's budget, cancelled billions in already-authorized grants for clean air, water, and climate resilience, and repealed the 2009 endangerment finding underpinning US climate regulation. These actions represent the largest rollback of climate policy in U.S. history.

It's important to note, though, this isn’t the first time the EPA’s faced massive hurdles. Under Reagan, Ruckelshaus was brought back to lead the EPA because his predecessor, Anne Gorsuch (yes, mother of Supreme Court Justice Neil Gorsuch) had almost entirely depleted the EPA by asking Congress to cut the agency's budget and halt enforcement activities.

So, what can you do? First, understand this isn’t some boring administrative issue. It directly impacts your health and that of your loved ones. Know where your reps stand on appropriations to the EPA and what they’re doing to support it. Make sure to give love to state and local environmental agencies, too. 

The Agency rose from the ashes before. With your help, it can do so once again.
